block_node.block_desc:
Arbitrate memory transactions for one or more Memory Channel blocks.
Ports burstReq and burstDone arbitrate requests from Memory Channel blocks. Set the Number of masters parameter to reflect the number of memory channels in your design.
Interconnect arbitration, Bandwidth, and other parameters can be changed in the Advanced section. In the Performance tab, metrics can be visualized after running a simulation.

Model the transfer of register values between processor and FPGA.
Each pair of input and output ports with the same name represent a register. On the FPGA side (HW) each port interfaces directly with the FPGA logic. On the processor side (SW) each port interfaces directly with a Register Read block if the register direction is configured to read, or with a Register Write block if the register direction is configured to write. Alternatively IO Data Source or IO Data Sink blocks can be used instead of Register Read or Register Write blocks when there is no processor in the system.
Add or remove registers by using the New and Delete buttons, respectively. Arrange the order of the registers using Move Up and Move Down buttons. To change the Name, Direction, Data Type and Dimension for a register, use the Edit button. Set register Direction to Read when the processor reads from the register, or to Write when the processor writes to the register. Set register Data Type and Dimension to match the values in the Register Read or Register Write blocks.

Model memory accesses as read and write bursts.
Data, CtrlIn and CtrlOut ports read and write data. burstReq and burstDone ports manage requests to the Memory Controller.
Burst length, Bandwidth, FIFO depth and other parameters can be changed in the Advanced section. In the Performance tab, metrics can be visualized after running a simulation.

Model interrupts from FPGA to processor.
Each pair of input and output ports with the same name represent an interrupt. On the FPGA side (HW) each input interfaces with a boolean signal from the FPGA, or an event from an Event Source or Memory Channel blocks. On the processor side (SW) each output connects to a Task Manager event input port.
Add or remove interrupts by using the New and Delete buttons, respectively. To change the priority of interrupts, arrange their order using the Move Up and Move Down buttons. Change the Name and Trigger Type of an interrupt by editing the value in the table. Set the interrupt Trigger Type to Rising Edge if the interrupt is coming from FPGA logic. Set the interrupt Trigger Type to SoC event if the interrupt is coming from Event Source block or Memory Channel block.

Read data from a memory-mapped register of a hardware logic IP core.
The block interfaces with a Register Write block and outputs the read data.
Set the Output data type and Output vector size parameters to match the equivalents in the register being read.

Generate read or write requests to memory as a dummy master. This block can be used to model the impact that another master has on your application without explicitly designing that master.
The block outputs memory request signals which should be connected to the burstReq and burstDone ports of a Memory Controller block. These signal lines do not transmit data.
The Burst length parameter is derived from the Burst size and Controller Data Width specified in the Hardware Implementation Pane.
In generated code, this block outputs uniformly distributed traffic request signals. In simulation, when 'Allow simulation-only parameters' is selected, this block provides more control than the generated code. Set the Random time between bursts parameter to specify the min and max values between bursts.

Model memory transfers from AX4-stream to software as write bursts.
wrData, wrCtrlIn and wrCtrlOut ports write data from stream. rdData, rdEvent and rdDone ports read data from software using Stream Read block.
Burst length, Bandwidth, FIFO depth and other parameters can be changed in the Advanced section. In the Performance tab, metrics can be visualized after running a simulation.

Model memory transfers from software to AX4-stream as read bursts.
wrData, wrEvent and wrDone ports write data from software using Stream Write block. rdData, rdCtrlIn and rdCtrlOut ports read data from stream.
Burst length, Bandwidth, FIFO depth and other parameters can be changed in the Advanced section. In the Performance tab, metrics can be visualized after running a simulation.

Model random access memory transfers as read and write bursts.
Data, CtrlIn and CtrlOut ports read and write data.
In the Performance tab, metrics can be visualized after running a simulation.

Model video frame buffer memory transfers as read and write bursts.
Data, CtrlIn and CtrlOut ports read and write data.
Burst length, Bandwidth, FIFO depth and other parameters can be changed in the Advanced section. In the Performance tab, metrics can be visualized after running a simulation.
